summary: The run reached Hexaghost with a functional but offense-heavy 16-card deck and was reduced to 3 HP before the final lethal sequence. The clearest immediate error was continuing to spend actions on setup or ending turns while additional defense was legally available at critical HP; an earlier contributor was accepting and retaining the Doubt curse.

lessons.title: At critical HP, take available defense before setup
lessons.situation: When HP is already in single digits and the enemy is attacking or the next hit is dangerous, especially when a block card remains playable.
lessons.lesson: Prioritize immediate block over Armaments, attacks, or ending the turn. Do not leave playable defense unused unless the combat can be ended safely or the block is clearly unnecessary.
evidence_points: On turn 12 at 6 HP, after playing Defend+ and Armaments+, the agent ended the turn with another Defend+ still legal and 1 energy remaining.
The next logged state began at 3 HP, showing that the turn-ending choice left almost no survival margin.
On turn 11 at 11 HP with Hexaghost attacking, the agent repeatedly chose Defend+, demonstrating that defensive cards were available and legal in this phase.
lessons.reasoning: The exact incoming damage is not logged, so the counterfactual cannot be proven, but the sequence shows a high-risk pattern: after reaching 6 HP, the agent spent energy on setup and then declined a remaining block. At that point survival should take precedence over improving future cards.

lessons.title: Avoid retaining optional curses without an immediate removal plan
lessons.situation: When an event offers gold in exchange for a permanent curse and there is no confirmed way to remove that curse soon.
lessons.lesson: Prefer declining the curse unless the gold is essential and removal is realistically available; if accepting it, prioritize removing the curse rather than another card.
evidence_points: At floor 13, the agent chose to gain 175 gold and become cursed with Doubt despite having a Disagree alternative.
The shop afterward removed a Strike, while the final 16-card deck still contained Doubt.
Doubt appeared in the Hexaghost hand on turn 14, where it occupied a draw alongside Bash+, Strike+, and Rampage+.
lessons.reasoning: The curse was not temporary: it remained in the final deck and appeared during the boss fight. The trajectory does not prove that Doubt caused the loss, but accepting it created persistent draw dilution and left a removable liability in the final build.

lessons.title: Be selective about adding more attacks after early damage density is established
lessons.situation: When several early rewards have already added attacks and the offered alternatives include defense, scaling, utility, or skipping.
lessons.lesson: Prefer a defensive or scaling card, or skip the reward, rather than repeatedly adding situational attacks that do not improve boss survivability.
evidence_points: The agent added Rampage, Pommel Strike, Cleave, and Whirlwind during Act 1, while the final deck also retained three Strikes, Bash+, and Rage.
At floor 5, Cleave was chosen over Evolve, and at floor 10, Whirlwind was chosen over Iron Wave, Limit Break, or skipping.
The final deck had four Defends but no newly added defensive card; the additional cards were predominantly attacks or attack support.
lessons.reasoning: The final deck had substantial attack density, yet the boss sequence still ended with the player at 3 HP. This suggests future rewards should be evaluated more for survivability and scaling than for adding another immediate damage option, particularly once the deck already has multiple attacks.
